clue.text: A soldier found it soon after midnight in Milan

indicators.note: the words before 'in Milan' are placed inside the city's name

parts.note: the Italian city's name taken as written
taken as written
one o'clock in the morning, written 1 AM, read as I AM

explanation.surface: A soldier turns up in Milan in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soon after midnight' is one o'clock, written 1 AM, with the figure read as the letter I; 'in' sets this and 'it' inside the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a citizen army, and each member of it is a part-time soldier.

clue.text: Club member's first to introduce one

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word member's is used

parts.note: an ace is the card counting as one

explanation.surface: A club's leading member brings in a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy spiked club used as a weapon in medieval times.

clue.text: Some illumination provided, in case

parts.note: a light housed inside a protective glass-sided box, read as 'just in case' but meaning literally in a case

explanation.surface: A little light kept handy just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp is a flame or bulb enclosed in a glass-sided case.

clue.text: What you will play?

parts.note: Shakespeare gave one comedy the alternative title 'What You Will', so the phrase names a play rather than asking a question

explanation.surface: Asking someone which piece they intend to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's comedy about Viola and Orsino carries the subtitle 'What You Will'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy was subtitled What You Will, so the play is literally that title.

clue.text: Probes upset girl in neat turnout

indicators.note: the girl's name goes inside the rearranged word neat
a turnout is a clearing out, so the letters of neat are turned out of order
in a down clue upset turns the girl's name upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Feelers sense a girl upset at a tidy turnout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the girl's name upside down in a down clue; 'turnout' scrambles 'neat'; 'in' sets the turned name inside the scrambled word.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feelers are sensory probes on its head.

clue.text: Descendant of an executed tycoon

indicators.note: an executed person is beheaded, so the first letter of the word for tycoon is cut off

parts.note: a magnate is a tycoon, a powerful business figure

explanation.surface: Heir of a business mogul who was put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' means beheaded: MAGNATE loses its head, M.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a relative traced through the male line, a descendant of the same forefather.

clue.text: Look' closely on hearing a mole here

indicators.note: on hearing means the word is taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Someone squinting at a burrowing animal they heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like the burrowing animal; here it is a stone breakwater. The stray apostrophe after 'Look' is a scanning blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a harbour breakwater or jetty, a structure jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Make a limited subscription by letter

definitions.meaning: to subscribe a document with just one's first letters rather than the full signature
the first letter of a name or word

explanation.surface: Signing up for a little by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing with only the first letters of one's name is a short signature; a single letter starting a word is also so called.

clue.text: In stony soil, pitch represents danger

parts.note: a ship that pitches rocks to and fro

indicators.note: represents read as re-presents, the letters of danger set out afresh

explanation.surface: Throwing a pitch on rocky ground is hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represents' rearranges DANGER into GARDEN. 'In' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden built of boulders and alpine plants is a patch of deliberately stony ground.

clue.text: Music-maker's collapse

definitions.meaning: to fold up in sections, like a bellows

explanation.surface: A musician has fallen down.
explanation.definitionFit: The bellows instrument folds up as it is played, so its name is also a verb for crumpling in pleats.

clue.text: One second inside 'current record

indicators.note: inside places the first pieces within the abbreviation for current

parts.note: DC is direct current
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Just a moment within the present record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present'; it is electric current, DC.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat circular plate.

clue.text: Brew this ale, perhaps — about right for the table

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the letter for right
perhaps hints that the letters of the opening words may be put another way

explanation.surface: A recipe suggesting brewing some beer for the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BREW THIS ALE; 'about' wraps those letters around R. It is a cheese dish, sometimes made with ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese melted on toast is a savoury dish served at the dining table.

clue.text: From Nashville, a fine tobacco

indicators.note: From means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Good tobacco sourced from Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across NashvilLE A Fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is sold and smoked as dried leaves, so the plant's foliage names it.

clue.text: Chewing the rag in tent?

indicators.note: chewing mangles what is chewed, so the letters of rag in tent are jumbled

explanation.surface: Gossiping away while camping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chewing' rearranges RAG IN TENT, and 'chewing the rag' is British slang for idle chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing the rag is slang for gossiping, the same as chattering idly.

clue.text: Remarkable sign in female being embraced by friend

indicators.note: the other pieces are held inside the word for friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a hen is a female bird
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A notable portent in a woman hugged by a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' only joins female and sign; 'being embraced by' puts both inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary or outstanding is called remarkable.

clue.text: Masterful type embraces new church — a' trusty supporter

indicators.note: embraces means the word for masterful type holds the next pieces

parts.note: a he-man is a domineering macho type

explanation.surface: A strong man adopts a new church as a loyal follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masterful type' is a macho strongman; 'embraces' sets new and church inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal follower or right-hand man is a faithful aide.

clue.text: Old stableman lacking aspiration?

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy H sound, so the letter H is dropped

parts.note: hostler is an old form of the word for an inn's groom

explanation.surface: A former groom with no ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition; it is the H sound, dropped from HOSTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn's groom who looked after travellers' horses, an old job title.

clue.text: Eg, do without one 'established sort of rose

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the musical note goes round the other pieces

parts.note: do is an example of a musical note in the sol-fa scale
the Roman numeral I is one
set means established or fixed

explanation.surface: Managing without a well-loved rose variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a verb; it is the sol-fa note. 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the note goes round one and established.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose type bred from a musk and China cross, named after the Noisette brothers.

clue.text: Square on the' table for game with family

parts.note: nap is a card game, short for Napoleon
kin means family

explanation.surface: A card table set for a family game.
explanation.walkthrough: NAP is a British trick-taking card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded square of cloth laid at each place setting for wiping lips.

clue.text: Show friendliness to a bird, for example

parts.note: to pat someone is a friendly gesture
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Being nice to a bird, say.
explanation.definitionFit: A model to copy is an exemplar.

clue.text: In the sovereign's residence, an oriental dance

indicators.note: In tells us the next word goes inside the royal residence

parts.note: a court is a monarch's household
E for east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: A dance from the East performed at the royal palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A courante is a running French dance of the baroque era.

clue.text: Unfamiliarity in all directions

indicators.note: in places one string of compass letters inside the other

parts.note: the four compass points north, east, west, south
three compass points again: north, east, south

explanation.surface: Feeling strange wherever one turns.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass letters are used twice over, one run set inside the other; the whole string reads as every direction at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fresh or never met before is to be unfamiliar.

clue.text: Artist turned up for recompense

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter arrived to claim payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived'; it reverses DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a payment given in return for services.

clue.text: Incomparable, but lacking fixtures

explanation.surface: A team that is peerless but has no games.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal; also, read literally, without any sporting fixture.

clue.text: Moves a boat along the river banks?

definitions.meaning: lines or tiers like the banks of oars on a galley

explanation.surface: Someone sculling along past the riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Propelling with oars; and lines or tiers are banks, as in banks of oars.

clue.text: Where malefactors move around?

definitions.meaning: slang for prison, where criminals are held

explanation.surface: Asking where wrongdoers wander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is old British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail, where criminals are kept; also to mix or agitate.

clue.text: Born in Toulon, died 'in penury

parts.note: the French for born, in its feminine form, is née

explanation.surface: A Provençal native who died poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe before 'in' is a scanning blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty is want, a lack of means.

clue.text: Extremely bright, are these wild creatures

indicators.note: wild means the letters run wild into a new order
the extremes of bright are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Admiring very colourful wild animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives B and T from bright; 'wild' rearranges them with ARE THESE. They are African antelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Large African antelopes are animals, so creatures.

clue.text: Sound connections for one with exceptional vision

indicators.note: Sound signals the word for connections is heard, not written

parts.note: links are connections

explanation.surface: Good links help someone see clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild cat is proverbial for sharp sight, hence lynx-eyed.

clue.text: Would-be salesman's inert consultant? On the contrary

indicators.note: read 'inert' as in ERT, consultant inside; on the contrary reverses this, so those letters go inside the consultant

parts.note: an adviser is a consultant
split as in plus ERT, the ERT being the piece placed

explanation.surface: A salesman's idle adviser? Quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inert consultant' reads as 'in ERT, consultant' (consultant inside the letters); 'On the contrary' flips that, so the letters go inside the consultant instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter of goods seeks buyers, hoping to sell.
